transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Um, I’m here because, well, after my shifts as a cashier, I just keep buying these huge takeout orders. Like, I'll order enough burgers, fries, chicken, and desserts for a whole family. And I'll just sit there... and I eat almost all of it myself before I even go home.
While you’re eating these large amounts, do you feel unable to stop or control what or how much you’re eating?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Um, once I take that first bite, it just feels like something in me clicks off. I'll actually be sitting there telling myself, 'Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more,' but... I just can't. My hands just keep reaching for the next thing in the bag. I really don't have any control over it once I start.
How often do these episodes of eating unusually large amounts happen?

Well, for the last several months, it’s been happening probably three or four nights most weeks. Honestly, I can’t remember a single week since the foreclosure calls started where I didn’t do it at least once.
How much emotional distress do these eating episodes cause you afterward?

Um, I guess it causes a lot. I'm not really sure how to measure it or describe it, honestly. I just... I feel really terrible about myself when it's over and I'm sitting in my car with all the empty wrappers. I don't really know what else to say about the distress part, but yeah, it definitely upsets me a lot.
After these eating episodes, do you ever deliberately do something to prevent weight gain?
No, I don't do anything like that. I don't throw up or take pills or exercise for hours or anything. I just... I just sit there and feel awful about it, but I don't try to undo it.
